title: #16 Films
prompt: For children, using films to study is as important as studying literature. To what extent do you agree?

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: Films provide learning about the world.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: Films provide learning about the world.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: Films help children understand emotions and social life.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: Films help children understand emotions and social life.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: Films are not as good as books because they miss details and cannot teach about feelings.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: Books are better than films because they help children use their mind and build creativity.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: Books are better than films because they help children use their mind and build creativity.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: Films provide a rich, visual learning experience by showing different cultures and life situations.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: Films provide a rich, visual learning experience by showing different cultures and life situations.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: Films help children develop emotional understanding and empathy by allowing them to relate to characters' struggles.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: Films help children develop emotional understanding and empathy by allowing them to relate to characters' struggles.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: Films are limited in the information they can teach, often prioritizing entertainment over deep learning, which means children may lack detailed knowledge.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: Films are limited in the information they can teach, often prioritizing entertainment over deep learning, which means children may lack detailed knowledge.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: Reading books enhances imagination and deep thinking because it requires the reader to build the world and characters in their mind.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: Reading books enhances imagination and deep thinking because it requires the reader to build the world and characters in their mind.

modelPlan.focus: Explore the role of films as an educational tool for children, comparing and contrasting it with traditional literature.
keyArguments: Films provide visual and engaging ways to learn, enhancing comprehension and empathy.
While films offer unique benefits, literature fosters deeper analytical skills and imagination.
